newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner in U.S. offshore air base project.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner in U.S. offshore air base project.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA said on Monday it had been awarded, subject to final negotiations, a contract to prepare a feasibility study for the world's first offshore air base for the U.S. Navy.
The initial multi-million dollar contract would take 18 months to complete, company spokesman Paul Emberley said. He declined to put a value on the deal.
Industry sources said construction of the giant three-platform structure would be worth at least $5 billion.
"We have been awarded the contract by the U.S. Navy subject to final negotiations. We hope to have something concrete in the next week or so," Emberley said.

The strategic defence project, dubbed Sea Base, comprises three semi-submersible platforms linked together and self-propelled, and would be large enough to land fixed-winged aircraft up to McDonnell Douglas C-17 in size and have accommodation for 10,000 troops.
Emberley said Kvaerner had patented the special links between the platforms, which had been developed to compensate for the effects of wave motion in open sea.

Construction of the structure would largely take place in the United States with American giant Boeing as sub-contractor. Kvaerner beat off bids from U.S. companies Brown & Root and McDermott International.

The London-based group has a strong business in the offshore oil and gas sector and is one of four multi-national partners in the Sea Launch project, which is building the first offshore satellite launching platform.
"Kvaerner has developed a strong reputation for innovation as is shown by Sea Launch, which is nearing the final stages of construction," Emberley said.
"Sea Base is another innovation nearing reality, which continues to use and develop our marine technology skills. It's a Kvaerner-led initiative and innovation."
